errors: No mathematical errors, since there are no computations.

Historically questionable characterisation: the 'Katze, Liebe' renaming attitude is attributed critically to Dedekind. Yet the dictum that the primitives could be called anything ('Tische, Stühle, Bierseidel') is famously Hilbert's own (attributed to 1891). Dedekind expressed a similar view only privately (letter to Lipschitz, 1876). Hilbert's criticism here seems aimed at a dogmatic insistence on avoiding ordinary names, not at the implicit-definition idea itself. This is a tension worth noting rather than an error.

results.what: Ordinary calculation (forcing identities) is a special case of the axiomatic method.
results.modern_name: Equational/algebraic reasoning as formal deduction from axioms (equational logic)
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert's axiomatic programme generally (c. 1899–1905 onward); equational logic formalised later (Birkhoff 1935)

results.what: Methodological maxim that the 'how' of a proof matters (purity of method), linked to proofs with or without the Archimedean axiom.
results.modern_name: Purity of method / reverse-mathematics-style analysis of axioms needed

results.what: Critique of one-sided methodological dogmas: Kronecker's finitism about irrationals, Holzmüller's calculus-free elementary methods, von Staudt's and Lagrange's avoidance of figures, Méray's anti-geometric arithmetisation, Dedekind's renaming.
results.modern_name: Methodological pluralism; defence of intuition and figures alongside axiomatics
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert's lecture-notebook views, discussed by Corry, Toepell, Hallett/Majer

results.what: Unity of science: axiomatisation is an imposition of unity on facts; the separation of geometry from physics is an arbitrary abstraction; 'there is only one science'.
results.modern_name: Hilbert's empiricist view of geometry as a natural science; unity of science via axiomatics
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert (lectures c. 1905, 'Axiomatisches Denken' 1917/18); documented by Corry

deep.surprise_reason: The material matches Hilbert's known notebook aphorisms on axiomatics, intuition and the unity of science. Two details are mildly notable. One is the explicit claim that calculation is a special case of 'my axiomatic method'. The other is the critical lumping of Dedekind's 'cat, love' renaming with Kronecker's and Méray's dogmas, given that Hilbert's own 'tables, chairs, beer mugs' dictum expresses the same idea. No mathematical result is involved.
